images.title: A tilted square projects to a rectangle
images.purpose: Shows a square card hinged on the floor and tilted so its far side is 3 cm up, and its projection, a 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. One oblique 3D scene in the centre: a pale grey floor, a tilted card above it and its projection on the floor directly under it.
images.exact_structure: Floor: a large pale grey parallelogram. Card: a square of side 5 cm filled semi transparent teal #0072B2; its near edge lies on the floor (the hinge), its far edge raised 3 cm above the floor. Two thin dashed grey vertical lines drop from the two raised corners straight down to the floor. Projection: the rectangle on the floor with the hinge as one side and the feet of the dashed lines as the far corners, filled amber #E69F00, with small right angle marks at its two hinge corners. Labels: '5 cm' on the hinge, 'card side 5 cm' on one slanted card edge, '3 cm up' on one dashed line, '4 cm' on the matching floor edge, and under the scene '5 cm by 4 cm rectangle'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Tilted about one side, a square projects to a rectangle: the tilted sides shrink to √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm.
images.description: Shows a square card hinged on the floor and tilted so its far side is 3 cm up, and its projection, a 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle.
images.context: Concept T10.C2; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Parallel sides stay parallel; never a trapezium.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the card and its projection in one scene is what makes the shrink of only the tilted sides clear.
